title: The Stash: profile as a treasure chest
what: Where everything that is yours lives once Library means the story shelf: gems, my stories, badges and stamps, steps, friends, walk journal, settings. Gems keep their own tab (B, decided Nov 26): the Stash links to Victoria’s Gem Hub. A (gems inside the Stash) and C (split by job) stay as switches for the record. Notes: names, what is there today, A vs B vs C. Research: how 15 apps do it, and the rules a profile must meet.
author: melissa

title: Everyday Story City
what: The whole app after the first-time tour: Today, the feed, the map, the library, You, gems, a full story to its ending, reminders and the trial. Journeys jump to a persona, Team Options switch open questions, Reviewer shows where each choice came from, and Type tunes fonts and colours.
author: melissa

title: Narrator text in real stories
what: Tales from the Incident and Dictators Laundromat in the app reader: narrator lines appear in sync with the real voiceover (Incident timed from the Audio matched to paragraphs data), no lone last words. Three layouts (full page, text window, over picture) and characters five ways (A–E), switched inside.
author: melissa

title: Type and colour tuning on real app screens
what: Archived Nov 25: the type and colour panel now lives in Everyday Story City (the Type button in its top bar). Live controls for every text role (story and chapter titles, eyebrows, body, chat bubbles, buttons, captions): weight, size, type scale, case, line height, spacing and colour, plus colours for backgrounds, cards, buttons and bubbles (Brand jewel or Today’s app in one tap). Shown on Library, Story, Chapter, Map and Paywall with real story covers. Copy as CSS, JSON or a guidelines table; the link keeps your setup.
author: melissa

title: How do you like to explore?
what: The select-all screen after sign-up, 9 ways to pick (switch inside, A–I), plus 4 heading options: playing cards, gems, fog over a real map, constellation, Bookerton chat, passport stamps, potion brew, Explorer card, living street. Each ends on what your picks unlocked.
author: melissa

title: Creator Tools: map + script
what: Two ways (switch inside): a story map you can edit (one row per stop, readable names, drag a choice's dot to link chapters, undo, find and highlight) and a Script tab (coloured as you type, insert buttons, type → to pick a chapter, drop many files at once). Plus Play: test the story on a phone from any chapter. EN / FR check. Real stories: Alice Through The Tear, Frightnight Ghost Tours, The Summons.
author: melissa

title: Gem map pins
what: Gems on a real Edmonton map, every version in one place: V1 the options lab, V2 Victoria's build, V3 Melissa's copy (Text glow, Quarter haze, create button). Switch versions in the Versioning rail.
author: melissa

title: Gem map pins V2
what: Victoria's gem art on Melissa's Edmonton map. Filter turns the top bar into a legend plus a gem roller. Slide-outs: Melissa original, Prompt, Image, Corner. Navigate and save for later stay on the Victoria versions.
author: victoria

title: First story flow
what: Two flows (switch inside). B, story first (default): welcome, “How do you walk?”, straight into The Summons, a two-page trial offer after chapter 1, an unlock with the in-story step-counting ask and an equal “I’m at home” button, “Save your story?” and one nudge ask, the cliffhanger offer (or walk 500 steps tomorrow), the finish, then Home and the tour. A: the Nov 12 proposal. Tester panel jumps to any step.
author: melissa

title: Story progress
what: Eight ways to show how far you are in a story (switch inside, A–H): dots, fog path, bar with “about X left”, bookmark ribbon, branch map, three acts, chapter ring, passport stamps. Play The Summons in the phone to see how each copes when a choice makes the story shorter.
author: melissa

title: Approved UI library
what: Page anchor with Original kept. Tools + Look/Move. Gem category selector + filters.
author: victoria

title: App screen catalog
what: Device screenshots of major screen types (welcome, FTUE, home, feed, map, profile, story overview, debug). Capture timestamps + build for light version control; download PNGs.
author: victoria

title: Daily Side Quests
what: Filled-map leave flow: end-batch stats + training-hub step land. Share beside like; next opposite username.
author: victoria

title: Location Gems hub
what: Page anchor: Original + Mist/Drift/Bloom flowy overlays. Dual shade on Tinted.
author: victoria

title: Day reached — streak overlay
what: Day-reached celebration with colour-wheel accent tester; phone-only embed.html for Approved UI.
author: victoria

title: Golden Path Nov 13: pick by letter
what: Six questions for Friday's Golden Path meeting, each as A / B / C phone mockups side by side with Melissa's pick marked (switch inside): when to force sign-up, asking again after “Not now”, what Start asks in the first real story, the explore browse map, the treadmill map, and the sample story's name.
author: melissa

title: Social media posts
what: 27 Instagram and TikTok post ideas to get new people walking their first story, each as a clickable mock-up: carousels, stories with poll, quiz and slider stickers, and reels. Includes the Instagram ideas from Help me choose a story, which link across.
author: melissa

title: Lock screen and widgets: the story keeps walking with you
what: A chapter of The Summons outside the app: a lock-screen Live Activity with distance and a changing story line, the Dynamic Island, a watch face, and home-screen widgets for your next walk (gems nearby, a tiny map, a gentle “Pick a Walk”). Switch surfaces inside; iPhone and Android, with a Tour.
author: melissa

title: Story Tools
what: Gadgets a story or whimsy walk can hand you, each introduced by Wren. Riddle Lock, Cipher Wheel, Compass Only, Sigil Walk, Field Guide, Sticker Book, Pass the Pen, Sound Catcher, Whisper Drop, Echo Answer, Then and Now (story-specific), Remix Relay (maybe), plus new ideas: Case Card, Silhouette Match, Field Notes, Evidence Board and Clue Courier. Five photo tools Melissa cut are folded at the bottom. Open one directly with ?v=<tool>.
author: melissa

title: Walk postcard + tomorrow's walk
what: Right after a chapter: a postcard builds itself (route, photo, one line, the gem you found) and you pick tomorrow's walk. Two orders (switch inside): postcard first, or plan first. Three postcard styles, the route's start blurred for privacy, and a Sunday weekly recap.
author: melissa

title: Play together
what: The Summons with friends, two ways (switch inside): pass one phone around, with roles, group votes and a team postcard; or everyone on their own phone, joining with a 4-letter code, each seeing a different clue, then a team finale.
author: melissa

title: Armchair preview: try it from your couch
what: For new players at home: 2 minutes of The Summons indoors, then a clear free-trial explainer, then “walk it for real tomorrow”. Two versions (switch inside): paywall straight after the cliffhanger, or one more taste first (crack the seal code in a casebook keypad).
author: melissa

title: Help me choose a story
what: Sixteen ways to match a new player to a first story from one start screen. Instagram: rooms, doors and lit-window carousels, first lines, poll-sticker chain, swipe-with-sound, card draw, Door of the Day and blind date. App: fork in the road, swipe deck, story chart and Venn, how long have you got, let a friend choose, a stranger who interviews you in chat, and walk thirty steps to open an envelope. Every result names you ("The Lamplight Wanderer") before the story.
author: melissa

title: Whimsy Walks
what: 22 walks + 12 quests from the Whimsy Walks board. Home picks for you: tonight's walk (changes daily), a 2-minute quest, 3 for right now, then all walks in sideways rows. Every walk ends with a shareable keepsake image and a hand-off into a real Story City story (its real opening lines, chapter 2 already part-walked). Cards remember what you've walked; seven walks open a sealed letter.
author: melissa

title: Fog mode: walking clears the map
what: The map starts in fog and walking clears it. Two views (switch inside): the chapter map as it looks in the app, or your home map filling in over the week. Vote on your favourite fog look inside.
author: melissa

title: New website concept
what: storycity.app reimagined in the jewel palette: the page is a walk, a playable first chapter, your street as a story map, 219 real stories, city pages, creators, gifts and teams.
author: melissa

title: Map mode names poll
what: Vote on names for the three map modes, then see the results (switch inside). 11 responses: Steps, Path and Hunt lead.
author: melissa

title: FTUE sample story choices
what: Summons 1- then 2-reply beats. Tap-hand mirrored on the phrase start edge; on two replies it fades from one choice onto the other.
author: victoria

title: Claim CTA: pulse + soft glow
what: End-of-story claim button pulse. Embed mode for Approved UI (?embed=1).
author: victoria

title: Code Entry
what: The code at the end of The Summons, six ways: Glow # (numbers keypad), QWERTY, and ring dials – 5 letters, round or on a drum, or whole words (THE GREEN-EYE SHARP-TOOTH FIRE DRAKE), curved or on a drum. Switch versions with the chips at the top of the code screen. Turn the rings until it lines up in the outline and it sends itself.
author: melissa

title: Audio matched to paragraphs
what: Six narrated Story City stories with each paragraph timed to its audio, shown as a chat, a visual novel and a lines-to-audio timeline. Tap a paragraph to play from it; the line being spoken stays lit until the next one starts. The volume slider follows a squared curve, so halfway is a quarter of the gain.
author: brett

title: Visual novel reader on a phone
what: The chapter's featured image on top and the paragraph being spoken underneath, sized for a phone. The previous paragraph stays until the next one starts. Same six stories as Audio matched to paragraphs.
author: brett

title: Graphic novel reader – proto
what: Victoria's restyle fork of Brett's phone visual-novel reader: place background, character sprite slot, text frame, top-bar speed, and player. Same timed paragraphs and stories; Brett's folder untouched.
author: victoria

title: Story overview: audio preview
what: Side-by-side swipe carousel for Meet the cast. Place tip + solid debug toggle.
author: victoria

title: Onboarding – guide on Explore
what: App Explore Netflix layout. Summons portal+sprite on purple card. Explore dismiss slides right; overview slides up. Copy: missed the sample / learn the tools.
author: victoria

title: Decrypt the Artwork
what: Reader chapter with the glowing Decrypt the Artwork ticket. Tap it to open Decrypt the Puzzle, pick a colour, then Select colour.
author: victoria

title: Dragon's name: word jumble
what: Three empty slots and a tray of little tags, two of them decoys. Drag (or tap) the right tags into the slots to build sharp-toothed green-eyed fire-eater.
author: brett

title: Dragon's name: text entry
what: The app moment as specced: a text box with the hint "The dragon's full name". Close spellings of sharp-toothed-green-eyed-fire-eater are accepted.
author: brett

title: Narrated reader
what: A narrated chapter, three ways (switch inside): synced chat bubbles, a text story, or captions over the art.
author: melissa

title: Decrypt race
what: Tap Decrypt the Letter. One glowing dot pops up at a time somewhere on the pixelated picture. Hit 10 of them to clear the letter. You can zoom in.
author: victoria

title: The Decryptor
what: The Summons letter comes back pixelated. Three colour swatches point into it: photograph something nearby in the same colour family to clear each patch, get an accuracy score for each, and a shareable match card at the end.
author: melissa

title: Map modes
what: The chapter card's map, two versions (switch inside): Steps, Pin and Hunt; or always a pin, where the place the chapter needs is always on the map nearby.
author: melissa

title: First steps
what: The first-time tour, with two sample stories (switch inside): The Summons or The Knight.
author: melissa

title: Chat chapter
what: The opening of Operation COPY/WRITE told as a text-message thread, with typing indicators and crisp-E hijacking the chat.
author: brett

title: Glitch Lab
what: Seven hack and signal-loss effects for the chat chapter, one button each. Full hack chains them into crisp-E taking over the thread.
author: brett

title: The Remixer
what: crisp-E's remix tool at Loc 3i: three tabs of one-tap effects (Mix it, Shape it, Wreck it), colour and contrast grids, and a draggable Lens. Save unlocks after any 2 tools.
author: melissa

title: Remix a masterpiece
what: Stamp a photo onto a public-domain painting, then pixelate, smear and recolour it. Superseded by The Remixer.
author: brett
